title: Multiplexed Nanoparticle Protein Corona Enables Accurate and Precise Deep Plasma Proteomics
projectDescription: The Proteograph Product Suite, a multiplexed nanoparticle (NP) protein corona-based proteomics workflow, substantially improves the depth of detection of proteins by mass spectrometry (MS) by compressing the dynamic range of protein abundances. Here, we explore the quantitative performance of the Proteograph Product Suite and its applicability to large-scale studies.  Using multi-species spike-in experiments, we investigated fold-change accuracy, linearity, precision and the lower limit of quantification (LLOQ) for the Proteograph Product Suite in conjunction with multiple MS instruments. We also manufactured four distinct lots of NPs (each capable of supporting over 100,000 assays) and evaluated batch to batch reproducibility.
sampleProcessingProtocol: To assess reproducibility, the pooled plasma sample PC11 was processed with four distinct nanoparticle batches (AMS2, AMS9, AMS10, AMS12), each in quadruplicate. Peptides were analyzed on an Orbitrap Exploris 480, with one AMS12 replicate excluded due to outlier characteristics.
dataProcessingProtocol: DIA-MS data were processed using DIA-NN v1.8.1 in library-free mode, searching against a combined Human UniProt database without matching between runs. A 1% FDR threshold was applied at both precursor and protein levels. Precursor intensities were log₂-transformed, median-normalized, and aggregated to protein intensities using the MaxLFQ method (via the R package "iq"). Coefficients of variation (CVs) were calculated for proteins detected in at least three replicates, both within individual batches and across batches using one replicate per batch as reference.
